page: Amazon Web Services r8i.2xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is set at 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The processor features a 480 MB L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX, and Intel TME. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are not included, and no local NVMe storage is bundled, requiring the host to rely on networked storage over its 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded throughput, registering top 25% percentiles in Geekbench single-core scoring and single-threaded gzip compression at 34.01 GB/sec. Text processing workloads demonstrate top-tier execution, reaching the upper 10% bracket. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-threaded tests, land within median averages. In-memory data structures perform reliably, sustained by 15.16 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, text generation with medium-sized 7B parameter models falls into the bottom 25% percentile, indicating limited efficiency for mid-tier CPU-bound artificial intelligence inference.

From an infrastructure perspective, the high RAM density relative to core count delivers solid qualitative cost efficiency for workloads constrained primarily by memory capacity rather than raw compute scale. The lack of integrated local disks means input-output operations are constrained by network storage paths and the 4 Gbps baseline link. Given these architectural traits, this server profile fits memory-resident databases, distributed caching nodes, Redis clusters, and memory-heavy transactional backends.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro System. Equipped with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores paired with 64.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory and a 480 MB L3 cache. Advanced instructions such as AVX-512 and AMX are supported. The instance includes 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, zero local storage, and no GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-threaded capabilities and high-tier text processing performance, alongside average multi-core compute throughput and steady in-memory Redis processing at over 15 million operations per second. Memory-bound language model inference shows weaker throughput. The system is structurally aligned with memory-intensive workloads including Redis caching, in-memory databases, and high-memory transactional data operations.
